classification.difficultyReason: Use equal sides to form two equations, solve by substitution and interpret the common side length.

content.prompt: The length of the sides of a triangle are $2x-4$, $y-7$ and $2y-4x$. If the triangle is equilateral, find the length of a side.

answer.worked:
An equilateral triangle has three equal sides.

$$\begin{align*}2x-4&=y-7\\y&=2x+3\end{align*}$$

Equating the first and third side lengths and substituting for $y$:

$$\begin{align*}2x-4&=2y-4x\\2x-4&=2(2x+3)-4x\\2x-4&=6\\2x&=10\\x&=5\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}y&=2(5)+3\\y&=13\end{align*}$$

The side lengths are $2(5)-4=6$, $13-7=6$ and $2(13)-4(5)=6$. Hence the length of a side is $6$.
